text.en:
Kabir has a lot of marbles. He puts them in bags of 100, boxes of 10, and a few loose ones.
He has 2 big bags, 4 boxes and 7 loose marbles.
"How many marbles do I have in all?" he wonders.

A 3-digit number has hundreds, tens and ones.
In 247: the 2 is in the hundreds place (2 hundreds = 200), the 4 is in the tens place (4 tens = 40), and the 7 is in the ones place (7 ones = 7).
So 247 = 200 + 40 + 7.
The place of a digit tells its value. In 472 the 4 means 400, but in 247 the 4 means 40.
10 tens make 100. 10 hundreds make 1000.
Look at the number 247. It has three digits.
The first digit is in the hundreds place. Two hundreds is two hundred.
The middle digit is in the tens place. Four tens is forty. The last digit is in the ones place: seven.
Put them together: two hundred and forty-seven. The place decides what a digit is worth.

problem.en: Kabir has 2 bags of 100, 4 boxes of 10 and 7 loose marbles. How many marbles in all?

why.en: Hundreds + tens + ones make the number.

prompt.en: Your friend thinks the 4 in 247 means 4. How will you explain what it really means?

requiredIdeas.en: The 4 is in the tens place, so it means 4 tens, which is 40.
The place of a digit decides its value.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking every digit is worth only itself.

points.en: A 3-digit number has hundreds, tens and ones.
The place of a digit decides its value.
